job_0e09c7ad58b88c13: Postdoctoral Scholar-Fixed Term East Lansing, Michigan, United States Plant Research Laboratory Nat Science 10032674 Area of Interest: Research/Scientific Full Time/Part Time: Full Time (90-100%) Group: Fixed Term Academic Staff Union/Non-Union: Non-Union Show More Show Less Faculty/Academic Staff Opening on: Apr 13 2026 Closing at: Apr 13 2028 - 23:55 EDT Salary Commensurate with Experience College Of Natural Science 1121375 View favorites Position Summary The Michigan State University Department of Energy Plant Reseach Lab (MSU DOE-PRL) for a Postdoctoral Associate in research on plant endomembranes July 1, 2026. The postdoctoral associate will work under the guidance of Professor Federica Brandizzi, Hannah Distinguished Professor. The Brandizzi laboratory addresses fundamental questions in plant endomembrane biology, with a focus on how secretory organelles establish and maintain their function and morphology during growth and stress. These studies aim to enable the translation of fundamental discoveries to crop improvement. The position will be based at Michigan State University in East Lansing, Michigan. The primary responsibility of this position is to conduct research on the biology of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) using multidisciplinary approaches, including proteomics, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, genomics, and advanced live-cell imaging. Our research focuses on identifying and characterizing proteins required for ER functional homeostasis. In particular, we study the unfolded protein response (UPR), a conserved signaling pathway activated by the accumulation of misfolded proteins in the ER. Faculty on the clinical practice track hold multi-year appointments that align with a 12-month service period (July 1-June 30). Faculty with 12-month service periods are paid for 11 months of service over a 12-month period (July-June), meaning the equivalent of one month is available for paid time off. Clinical Practice track appointments are not eligible for tenure. Compensation provided by Children’s University Medical Group (CUMG) practice plan may provide eligibility for separate benefits offered by that organization. Other compensation associated with this position may include incentive through Children’s University Medical Group practice plan. Additional administrative responsibilities may be offered to a specific candidate with appropriate experience and qualifications which may result in an administrative supplement (ADS). The successful candidate will lead the development of a new Comprehensive Asthma Program at Seattle Children’s Hospital. Positive factors for consideration include, but are not limited to, candidates with leadership skills and/or clinical expertise in asthma. The faculty member will work collaboratively to build an inpatient, outpatient and community-based program that integrates clinical care with advocacy and research. POSITION SPECIFICS Tenured/Tenure-Line Associate Professor – Division of Epidemiology Department of Public Health Sciences, Penn State College of Medicine, Hershey, PA The Department of Public Health Sciences (PHS) at the Penn State College of Medicine announces a tenured or tenure-line faculty position at the Associate Professor level in the Division of Epidemiology for a qualified individual with expertise in infectious disease epidemiology. The mission of PHS is to advance health through the design, conduct, and analysis of population-based biomedical research—including clinical trials, observational research, health services research, and regulatory and translational science—supporting both basic science and clinical research, educating future generations of health professionals, and engaging with the community to improve health and well-being. We seek a highly collaborative researcher with experience in infectious disease epidemiology to conduct independent and team-based research. Interest in teaching is required, and experience teaching graduate-level courses is preferred. PHS comprises three academic divisions: Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Epidemiology, and Health Services and Behavioral Research. The department provides comprehensive infrastructure for faculty, the College, and Penn State Health, including expertise in biostatistics, study design, data management, research computing, project management, and finance and administration. PHS offers graduate programs including the PhD in Epidemiology, PhD in Biostatistics, Doctor of Public Health (DrPH), Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Science (MS) in Clinical Research, and Master of Professional Studies in Homeland Security with an option in Public Health Preparedness, as well as several graduate certificate programs. The ideal candidate will have an established, externally funded research program in infectious disease epidemiology, with particular strengths in sexually transmitted infections (STIs), HIV, and other emerging or re-emerging infectious threats. Strong candidates may focus on advancing understanding of the epidemiology, prevention, and clinical management of STIs; evaluating disparities in infectious disease burden across rural and urban communities; and improving public health surveillance, diagnostic practices, and access to testing and treatment. Scholarship that integrates epidemiologic methods with clinical, community-based, or health system–based research—such as assessing public health policy impacts, analyzing diagnostic and screening practices, addressing social determinants of infectious disease transmission, or informing health equity initiatives—is highly valued. Candidates with collaborative experience with public health agencies, development or evaluation of diagnostic tools, or translation of epidemiologic findings into interventions for health departments, clinics, or community partners are strongly encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will dedicate approximately 80% effort to research, 15% to teaching and mentoring, and 5% to service. A doctoral degree in epidemiology or a related discipline is required, along with a track record of scholarly activity

Position description Professor Henri Drake in the Department of Earth System Science at the University of California, Irvine is seeking a postdoctoral scholar for an NSF-funded project that aims to use computational models to investigate the role of ice sheets in the global Earth System, with a focus on advancing understanding of two-way feedbacks between the cryosphere (grounded ice sheets, floating ice shelves, ice bergs, and sea ice) and the ocean – and their role in global climate dynamics. The start date is very flexible, anytime from Jan 1, 2027 to Sep 1, 2027. The selected candidate will conduct cutting-edge research, including: Developing, running, and analyzing fully-coupled experiments using novel configurations of the Community Earth System Model (CESM3) with dynamic representations of the Greenlandic and Antarctic ice sheets, utilizing two-way synchronous coupling to the Community Ice Sheet Model (CISM3). Evaluating and calibrate newly implemented parameterizations for basal melt and calving Developing and applying new process-based diagnostics to evaluate the fidelity of the simulations, grounded in available remote sensing and in-situ observations. Running mechanism denial experiments to isolate the role of coupled feedbacks.  Position Summary The Kumar Lab in the Department of Otolaryngology at Washington University in St. Louis (WashU) is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Associate to join an NIH-funded research program investigating the cortical cellular and circuit mechanisms underlying hearing difficulties in noisy environments following noise-induced hearing loss. Our research integrates systems neuroscience, genetics, pharmacology, and computational approaches to understand how cortical circuits adapt to hearing loss and contribute to impaired auditory perception. The Kumar Lab employs a multidisciplinary experimental toolkit that includes: In vivo two-photon imaging of identified neuronal populations in awake mice, auditory behavioral assays, ex vivo brain-slice imaging and electrophysiology, chemogenetic and optogenetic circuit manipulation, Inducible conditional knockout mouse models, and Pharmacological interventions. The successful candidate will use these cutting-edge approaches to investigate the neural plasticity of cortical circuits associated with hearing deficits. This position offers an outstanding opportunity to conduct high-impact neuroscience research in a vibrant academic setting with access to state-of-the-art imaging, electrophysiology, and computational resources. The Kumar Lab is committed to fostering scientific excellence, collaboration, and the professional development of trainees.
